title: A build may give a template article its own address, date and byline on every CMS; a page's address, an author, a status and a count stay held
steps: S1: compareAgentInventory on a WordPress post moved from /how-the-gop-and-dems-differ-on-restaurant-issues/ dated 2021-09-27 to /our-cookie-club/ dated 2026-10-26, beside an unchanged page.
S2: the same with the page's slug changed; with the post's author changed; with the post made a draft.
S3: an EmDash posts entry whose slug and publishedAt change; an EmDash pages entry whose slug changes.
S4: a Joomla article whose alias, created, publish_up and created_by_alias change.
expect: S3: the posts entry passes; the page fails.
evidence: Local round 31 (25/10/2026, WordPress JA Restaurant): rewritten posts kept the template's slugs and its 27 September 2021 date.
fence: buildChangesOf (WP_FIXED_TYPES, WP_FIELDS, JOOMLA_FIELDS, EMDASH_DATE, identity.slug); maskBuildChanges in compareAgentInventory; BUILD_CHANGES_BRIEF

tests: an article's address and date are the build's on every CMS; a page's address, its count and its publication are not
